newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols flat to lower, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols flat to lower, trade thin.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt futures options were flat to slightly lower in thin speculative trade, dealers said on Thursday.

"What you're basically seeing is some guys putting on some stuff, just small little gambles, expiration plays, and probably liquidations since most of it is in the January," said one dealer on the floor of the Chicago Board of Trade.
January serial T-bond options expire on Friday. December T-bond futures expire at noon CST/1800 GMT.

Some of the larger plays of the day included: the sale of 1000 January 113 puts by a European bank, the purchase of 500 January 113 calls and 500 January 111 puts by a U.S. house, the sale of 1,000 January 112/113 combos by another, and the purchase of 1,000 March 112 puts by another, the dealer said.
At 1045 CST/1645 GMT, implied volatilities for February and March T-bond options were down roughly 0.10 percentage point each, at 9.5 percent and 9.9 percent respectively.
T-bond futures are unlikely to move significantly in the run-up to Christmas, said Josh Stiles, an analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc., making the purchase of volatility risky.
"I wouldn't be a buyer of vol right now, especially with the time horizon of end of year," he said. "The only thing I could hope for on the upside would be a modest oversold bounce."

Fundamentally, the market requires a better understanding of the U.S. economy in the fourth quarter, and specifically whether results suggest forward momentum into next year, he said. As a result, he expects March T-bond futures to hover near 112-12, which equates to a yield of 6.66 percent on the long bond.
One possible strategy in such a market might be to sell two-week straddles, he said.
In contrast, there is room for a surprise move in eurodollar futures volatility, although it is also unlikely before the end of 1996, he said.
"There's potential for a volatility move into the New Year because the sentiment is so deeply ingrained that the Fed is on hold for the foreseeable future," he said.
Stiles believes Fed comments suggest the U.S. economy is growing slightly faster than officials would like but that monetary policy will not change without a rise in inflation.
"That could easily happen and if it happens it's going to create a quick adjustment. But I don't think it's going to happen for the rest of this year," he said.
Dealers at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said trade in eurodollar futures options was thin and volatilities flat.
Implied volatility for March at-the-money eurodollar futures options was seen at 9.5/9.75 percent while June was trading at 13.5/13.75 percent.
"There hasn't been a lot of size coming into the options today. It's the holiday market," one dealer said.
